<abalone-tool>{"op": "write", "path": "summary.md", "content": "# Grant Summary

This R21 exploratory grant draft ($412,750 over 2 years, PI Dr. Marguerite Okonkwo-Hale) tests whether the timing of bright-light exposure at the end of night shifts—not total exposure—predicts daytime sleep onset latency in 60 night-shift nurses over 14 days of baseline actigraphy monitoring [L3-L15]. It then evaluates, in a randomized crossover design, whether blue-blocking glasses worn during the commute home cut sleep onset latency by at least 10 minutes versus sham lenses, with chronotype explored as a potential moderator [L17-L20]. The grant emphasizes significance for shift work disorder and nurse safety (sleep loss links to medication errors and burnout), is powered at 80% to detect the 10-minute effect, and acknowledges limitations including actigraphy inaccuracy, incomplete blinding, and single-site recruitment [L24-L35, L57-L60].
"}
